sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and purpose of the vocabulary tests
sections.what: Holds the one-line purpose and the imports for the work-unit tests, including the resolver and the vocabulary.
sections.why: The file's purpose is stated in its docstring: the benchmark join key is a fixed vocabulary because free text cannot be one.
sections.watch_out: If the resolver or the vocabulary moves to another module, these imports must change.

sections.name: TestTheVocabulary
sections.title: Vocabulary rules
sections.what: Checks that UNSPECIFIED is a member, that the list stays at twelve members or fewer, that every alias points to a real member, and that no alias points to UNSPECIFIED.
sections.why: UNSPECIFIED is the honest answer for a process that does not fit. The size limit stops the list growing into one entry per client wording. The alias rule keeps a deliberate non-match distinct from a failed lookup.
sections.watch_out: Adding an alias that points to UNSPECIFIED would break the test on purpose, because it would make a real non-match look like a failed lookup.

sections.name: TestResolution
sections.title: Label resolution rules
sections.what: Checks that known labels resolve to the right unit regardless of case, underscores, spaces or hyphens, that member names resolve to themselves, that an unknown label becomes UNSPECIFIED, that near misses are not matched, and that repeated lookups give the same answer.
sections.why: The docstrings say a wrong join is worse than no join, and that the table is exact on purpose because every entry is a judgement and a similarity threshold would hide that.
sections.watch_out: Loosening matching to accept similar wording would let a mining process join a field service cohort. These tests are the guard against that.

summary: Checks that the work-unit vocabulary, the fixed list of kinds of work used to compare processes, is well formed, and that free-text labels map to it exactly or become UNSPECIFIED.
purpose: Keeps benchmark comparisons honest by making sure processes are only grouped when their work units truly match.
why: The docstring says free text cannot be a join key, so a fixed vocabulary is needed. Tests also say a loose match would put unlike processes together and produce figures that look computed.
how: Checks that the enumeration includes UNSPECIFIED, has at most twelve members, that every alias points to a real member, and that no alias points to UNSPECIFIED. Then checks that known labels resolve, that case and punctuation do not change the result, that a member name resolves to itself, that unknown labels become UNSPECIFIED, that near misses are not fuzzy matched, and that resolution is deterministic.
inputs: Free-text labels, the WorkUnit enumeration, and the alias table in the schema package.
outputs: One WorkUnit member per label, or a pass or fail for each test.
risks: Adding an alias for a near-miss label can put unlike processes together. Fuzzy matching would be a regression the tests are meant to stop. The alias table is a set of judgements that need review.
debug: If a label resolves to the wrong unit, check the alias table in the schema package and the normalising rules in the knowledge normalise module. If a label that should match becomes UNSPECIFIED, check whether the label is in the alias table at all.
